subject: Inference serving discovery — AuroraHealth (cost & success criteria)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Courtney Li <c.li@aurorahealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-04-15T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inference serving discovery — AuroraHealth (cost & success criteria)

Hi Courtney / Tom —

Great to meet you both earlier. Summary from our 30-min discovery so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Quick context (what I heard)
- Current workload: ~2–3M short text queries/day (mix of chat prompts and summarization), typical request length 40–120 tokens, 95th percentile sequence ~320 tokens.
- Peak behavior: occasional bursts ~450–550 qps during morning triage windows.
- Current stack: calling a mixture of CloudVendorX hosted endpoints + some internal caching layer; no dedicated GPU fleet today.
- Pain: unit economics are highly variable month-to-month. They saw cost spikes when burst traffic forced smaller batches; 99th percentile latency and cost are the two main blockers for a live assistant rollout.
- Security: PHI concerns — preference for private network paths / VPC and SOC2 evidence.

Success criteria you outlined
- Predictable unit cost at scale (target: >30% reduction vs current baseline).
- P99 latency target: <=150ms for the assistant path during normal load; acceptable degradation during big bursts but with graceful fallback.
- No unredacted PHI exiting Aurora's VPC or shared training stores; audit logs and KMS integration required for any private deployment.

Operational constraints
- Open to latency-optimized batching/caching but need control over cache TTLs for sensitive content.
- Quantization openness: willing to evaluate 8-bit/4-bit if model output fidelity for clinical summarization is validated on a sample prompt set.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) You to share a representative 48-72hr anonymized workload sample (CSV) and a short list of ~10 critical prompts/labels for quality checks — you mentioned you can share this via Drive. (Attachment stub: aurora_workload_sample.csv)
2) Redwood to run a quick unit-economics sketch + latency profile for two options: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) and Redwood Private (VPC). We'll include assumptions about batch sizes and cache hit rates.
3) Follow-up SE deep-dive with Vivek to talk batching, KV caching, and quantization tradeoffs — target Wed/Thu next week.
4) Security questionnaire & SOC2 evidence exchange — you said procurement will want SOC2 summary; I’ll attach what we can share and route the formal questionnaire.

Proposed timeline
- Internal sketch & SE prep (us): 48 hours after we get the workload sample.
- SE deep-dive: propose Wed 2026-04-21 10:00am PT — let me know if that works.

Ballpark asks for you to confirm in reply
- Is the 2–3M/day volume correct?
- Are the PHI constraints limited to inference logs and not development/testing copies?
- Any procurement timeline targets (quarterly/PO/signed contract window)?

I'll attach a short SOC2 summary and a ballpark pricing PDF for context.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: aurora_workload_sample.csv, SOC2_summary_aurora.pdf, Redwood_ballpark_estimate.pdf
From: Courtney Li <c.li@aurorahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-04-15T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference serving discovery — AuroraHealth (cost & success criteria)

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches our notes. A few clarifications:
- Volume: 2.4M/day is the more consistent average; spikes up to ~520 qps for short periods (10–20 minutes) during morning triage.
- PHI: correct — inference requests will contain PHI. We cannot have persistent unencrypted copies outside our VPC; audit logs are required for every inference.
- Quantization: clinical QA is mandatory. We'll need a validation run on our 10 prompts before we greenlight 8-bit models.
- Procurement: we are working on a PO for early summer; procurement expects a pricing ballpark this month to build the budget.

I'll share the anonymized 72hr sample via Drive by EOD tomorrow and include the 10 QC prompts.

Courtney Li
Director, Clinical AI | Aurora Health
c.li@aurorahealth.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Courtney Li <c.li@aurorahealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-04-15T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference serving discovery — AuroraHealth (cost & success criteria)

Courtney — perfect, appreciate the confirmations. Next actions on our side:
1) I'll schedule the SE deep-dive with Vivek and include a short kickoff doc so we can validate batching targets (we'll run simulation at batch sizes 1/4/8 and with expected cache hit rates of 0/20/50%).
2) Jonas will run a quick ballpark unit-economics sheet (attachment: Redwood_ballpark_estimate.pdf) based on 2.4M/day and the peak profile you confirmed. It will include an expected per-token cost range for Dedicated vs Private and assumptions on tokenization.
3) I'll send the SOC2 summary now (attached) and open the formal security questionnaire request once we get procurement's contact.

Proposed SE slots (all PT): Wed 2026-04-21 10:00am, Wed 2026-04-21 2:00pm, Thu 2026-04-22 11:00am. Which is best for you?

If you can indicate any quality thresholds (e.g., max acceptable BLEU/ROUGE change or a human-review pass rate), we can include that validation in the 10-prompt run.

Thanks again — forwarding a short internal brief next.

Best,
Neha

Attachments: Redwood_ballpark_estimate.pdf, SOC2_summary_aurora.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-15T19:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: AuroraHealth discovery — scope for SE + pricing

Forwarding the thread from earlier today — Aurora Health (Courtney Li / Tom Reynolds). Quick notes for SE/pricing:
- Workload: ~2.4M/day, 95th token seq ~320, spikes to ~520 qps. They need P99 <=150ms for assistant flow.
- PHI: strict — all inference must be VPC/private path; audit logs + KMS required.
- Goals: 30%+ unit cost reduction vs their current CloudVendorX baseline; acceptable to test 8-bit quantized models only after QC on their 10 prompts.

Action items
- Vivek: can you run a microbench with our recommended kernels for their seq lengths assuming batch sizes [1,4,8] and a KV cache hit of 0/20/50%? Focus on tail latency and per-token GPU utilization. Also note any model-accuracy risks with 8-bit quant on summarization prompts.
- Jonas: please produce a 1-page unit-economics sketch for Dedicated vs Private using the attached workload sample (aurora_workload_sample.csv). Include bandwidth assumptions and cache savings scenarios.
- Marissa: track procurement timeline — they want a budget ballpark this month for a PO. I'll share the HubSpot deal after we have the econ sketch.

Attachments forwarded: aurora_workload_sample.csv

Thanks team — propose sync tomorrow morning for 20m to align outputs.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
